                     <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> 1.) so as the Scripture nameth 17. tho <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> leaves out 3. in two different Lines; it is not impossible that one person in so many years might have so many more Progenitors than another, supposing <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> designed to reckon all, which it is plain from his leaving out three Kings named in Scripture that he did not. 4. That ordinarily the Jews had two Names, sometimes three, all <ns0:hi>Iosiahs</ns0:hi> Sons had each of them two at least. <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> had also the Name of <ns0:hi>Levi, &c.</ns0:hi> This solves the difference from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 27. where <ns0:hi>Rhesa</ns0:hi> is said to be the Son of <ns0:hi>Zorobabel,</ns0:hi> when as <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 1.13. <ns0:hi>Zorobabel</ns0:hi> begat <ns0:hi>Abiud.</ns0:hi> That <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> was the Son of <ns0:hi>Terah</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Thara,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Terah</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Nachor,</ns0:hi> appeareth from <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 11.24. 26. That <ns0:hi>Saruch</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Sarug,</ns0:hi> was the Son of <ns0:hi>Reu</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Ragau,</ns0:hi> ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />peareth from <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 11.20. 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 1.25. that <ns0:hi>Reu</ns0:hi> was the Son of <ns0:hi>Peleg,</ns0:hi> (here called <ns0:hi>Phalec</ns0:hi>) and <ns0:hi>Peleg</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Eber,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Eber</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Sala</ns0:hi> appears from <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 11.18. 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 1.25. But in <ns0:hi>Genesis</ns0:hi> 11. we read, that <ns0:hi>Sala</ns0:hi> was the Son of <ns0:hi>Arphaxad v.</ns0:hi> 12. whereas he is here said to be the <ns0:hi>Son of Cainan,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Cainan</ns0:hi> is made the Son of <ns0:hi>Arphaxed.</ns0:hi> So as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> maketh <ns0:hi>Sala</ns0:hi> Grand<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />child to <ns0:hi>Arphaxad, Moses</ns0:hi> makes no mention of <ns0:hi>Cainan</ns0:hi> at all, but mentions <ns0:hi>Salah,</ns0:hi> as begotten by <ns0:hi>Arphaxad.</ns0:hi> Those who are curious to know what is said for the resolution of this difficulty, may read it largely both in <ns0:hi>Spanheims dubia Evangelica,</ns0:hi> and Mr. <ns0:hi>Pools Synopsis Criticorum.</ns0:hi> It is a difficulty which hath exer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cised many very learned Men, and I doubt whether ever any yet satisfied himself in the resolution of it. It is not probable that <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> should correct what <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> said, the best account I can give of it is, the <ns0:hi>Septuagint</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 11, 12. have it just as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> here hath it, and it is certain, that <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> in his quotations out of the old Testament, doth generally follow the <ns0:hi>Septuagint,</ns0:hi> (being the translation most in use among them) <ns0:hi>Beza</ns0:hi> tells us of an ancient Copy of the <ns0:hi>Gospel</ns0:hi> he had, which mentioneth no <ns0:hi>Cainan.</ns0:hi> The best of it is, that it is a matter of no great moment, for the Questi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on is not, whether <ns0:hi>Sala</ns0:hi> was the Son of <ns0:hi>Arphaxad,</ns0:hi> (for so he was, tho <ns0:hi>Arphaxad</ns0:hi> was his Grandfather, in the same sense that Christ is called the <ns0:hi>Son of Abraham,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Son of David,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Elizabeth</ns0:hi> the Daughter of <ns0:hi>Aaron ch.</ns0:hi> 1.1.) but whether he was the immediate Son of <ns0:hi>Arphaxad,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Cainan,</ns0:hi> whether <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> omitted <ns0:hi>Cainan,</ns0:hi> or some transcriber of <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> added <ns0:hi>Cainan</ns0:hi> out of the <ns0:hi>Septuagint</ns0:hi> (being then the current Translation among them) the last is most probable. For the other part of the <ns0:hi>Genealogy v.</ns0:hi> 36, 37, 38. it plainly agreeth with <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 5, 6, <ns0:hi>&c. &</ns0:hi> 6.10. So that I must profess I see no great difficulty to reconcile the Genealogies, admitting the one to give the Genealogy of <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> and the other, to give the Genealogy of <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi>; that indeed <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> was the Daughter of <ns0:hi>Heli,</ns0:hi> is not to be proved by Scripture, nor yet contradicted, but it is very probably judged so. And tho we cannot prove that <ns0:hi>Cainan,</ns0:hi> mentioned <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 36. was added out of some latter Copies of the <ns0:hi>Septuagint,</ns0:hi> yet it is more than probable it was so; which two things if we admit, I see no great difficulty remaining, but a fair agreement betwixt both the Evangelists. For I presume none will stumble at the alteration of some letter, or omission of some letter in a Name, or addition to it in the end; there is nothing more ordinary than that, when <ns0:hi>Names</ns0:hi> are men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned in several Languages.</ns0:note>
